onboarding.fdaBadge.label: No full disk access
onboarding.fdaBadge.tooltip: You don’t have to grant this, but Cmdr works much better with it: searching your whole drive, reading cloud folders, and changing files macOS keeps to itself. Click to look at the choice again.
onboarding.fdaBadge.ariaLabel: No full disk access. Open the full disk access step of onboarding.
onboarding.wizard.title: Cmdr onboarding
onboarding.wizard.stepTooltip: Step {step} of {mandatory}+1{note, select, remaining {, one optional step remains} last {, this is the last, optional step} other {}}
onboarding.stepFda.granted.title: You granted full disk access!
onboarding.stepFda.granted.body: Nice, that’s all Cmdr needs. Restart it now to start using everything.
onboarding.stepFda.granted.hint: Cmdr picks up the new permission on the next launch. Your spot in onboarding is saved, so you’ll land right back here.
onboarding.stepFda.alreadyGranted.title: Cmdr currently has full disk access
onboarding.stepFda.alreadyGranted.body: You can revoke it any time in {systemSettings}.
onboarding.stepFda.welcome.title: Welcome to Cmdr!
onboarding.stepFda.revoked.intro: It looks like you accepted full disk access before but then revoked it.
onboarding.stepFda.revoked.noAccess: The app currently has no full disk access.
onboarding.stepFda.revoked.ifIntentional: If that was intentional, click <deny>Deny</deny> and the app won’t bother you again.
onboarding.stepFda.revoked.ifNot: If it wasn’t intentional, consider allowing full disk access again. Here are the pros and cons:
onboarding.stepFda.firstAsk.lede: You probably just want to start using the app. Sorry to bother you with this first, but it’s needed.
onboarding.stepFda.firstAsk.explain: You see, Cmdr is a file manager, and it needs to access your disk to see all your files. macOS doesn’t automatically grant permission to this.
onboarding.stepFda.firstAsk.askPermissio: Would you like to give this app full disk access? Here’s what that means:
onboarding.stepFda.pro.label: Pro:
onboarding.stepFda.pro.body: The app will access your entire disk without nagging you for permissions to each folder like Downloads, Documents, and Desktop.
onboarding.stepFda.con.label: Con:
onboarding.stepFda.con.body: Full disk access is pretty powerful. It lets the app read any file on your Mac. Only grant this if you trust Cmdr. Cmdr uses this right respectfully, and is <sourceLink>source-available</sourceLink> if you feel unsure.
onboarding.stepFda.step2.ventura: Find Cmdr in the list and toggle it on
onboarding.stepFda.step2.older: Find Cmdr at the end of the list and toggle it on
onboarding.stepFda.step2.tip: Is Cmdr not in the list? Click the “+” button at the bottom, and choose Cmdr from your Applications folder.
onboarding.stepFda.postAction.intro: Cmdr needs to restart so the new permission takes effect.
onboarding.stepFda.postAction.body: When you’re ready, click <restart>Restart Cmdr</restart> below. If you change your mind, click <deny>Deny</deny> above instead.
onboarding.stepFda.openSettingsFailed: Cmdr couldn’t open {systemSettings}. Open it yourself, go to {privacyAndSecurity}, then {fullDiskAccess}, and turn on Cmdr.
onboarding.stepAi.bannerBody.granted: Thanks for granting full disk access! Now, the app can access your disk. Great!
onboarding.stepAi.bannerBody.denied: You chose not to enable full disk access. We respect that. You’ll then shortly get a few permission requests from macOS for Cmdr to access your Desktop, Downloads, and similar folders. Accept or reject these at will. You can change all of this later in your {systemSettings}.
onboarding.stepAi.bannerTitle.stuck: Cmdr doesn’t seem to have full disk access yet
onboarding.stepAi.bannerBody.stuck: You said you wanted to enable full disk access, but Cmdr doesn’t seem to have gotten it. You might need to restart the app (do it now, we’ll continue from here!), or go to your <settingsLink>{systemSettings} > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access</settingsLink> and find Cmdr, or manually add it with the little “+” button at the bottom.
onboarding.stepAi.welcomeLinux.title: Welcome to Cmdr!
onboarding.stepAi.welcomeLinux.subtitle: Let’s set up AI.
onboarding.stepAi.title: Now, let’s talk AI
onboarding.stepAi.intro: Cmdr has a bunch of AI features that you may want and may not want. AI is a controversial topic these days.
onboarding.stepAi.comparisonIntro: Here is how you do common actions with and without AI:
onboarding.stepAi.table.searchWithout: You type something like *fish*.ppt, and select the “after 1st of this month” filter.
onboarding.stepAi.table.searchWith: You say “my recent fish-related presentations”, agent sets your filters.
onboarding.stepAi.table.renameWithout: You set a rename pattern by hand in Multi-rename, then review and apply it.
onboarding.stepAi.table.renameWith: You say “add ISO date prefix”, agent sets your rename pattern, you review and apply at will.
onboarding.stepAi.table.selectWithoutBou: You press the key and type something like *.jpg,*.png,*.gif,*.heic,*.webp,*.jpeg, review and apply.
onboarding.stepAi.table.selectWithoutUnb: You open “Select files…” and type something like *.jpg,*.png,*.gif,*.heic,*.webp,*.jpeg, review and apply.
onboarding.stepAi.table.selectWith: You say “select all image files”, agent suggests a selection, you review and apply at will.
onboarding.stepAi.resumeCue: You picked this last time. Confirm or change below.
onboarding.stepAi.cloud.label: Yes, I want AI
onboarding.stepAi.cloud.help: Use any cloud provider with your own API key, or your own ollama/custom LLM. Configure it below.
onboarding.stepAi.local.label: Yes, I want AI, but I want it to be super private with a simple local model.
onboarding.stepAi.local.tooltip: The local model is significantly dumber than cloud models, and it takes up about 2 GB of space and some RAM and CPU at every use. In return, no data leaves your machine. Cmdr tries to ship updates so you can use the best small model that’s available. But if you want privacy and a decent model, running your own ollama server and setting it up with option Yes, I want AI below is your best choice.
onboarding.stepAi.local.note: Started downloading the local model in the background. You can finish onboarding now; the toast in the corner will keep you posted.
onboarding.stepAi.localTooltip: Local LLM requires Apple silicon. Cloud works on Intel.
onboarding.stepAi.missingKeyWarning: You’ve enabled AI but haven’t entered an API key. AI won’t work and you’ll see a warning. Please fix this above. Click “{nextLabel}” again to ignore this and go on.
onboarding.stepAi.cloudConsentOffNote: Cloud AI stays off until you allow it. You can do that later in Settings > AI.
onboarding.stepAi.off.label: Thanks but no thanks, no AI for me
onboarding.stepAi.off.help: Cmdr works fully without AI. You can turn it on later in Settings.
onboarding.localDownloadFailed.title: The local AI model didn’t finish downloading
onboarding.localDownloadFailed.body: Start it again from Settings › AI.
onboarding.stepBeta.title: Help improve Cmdr!
onboarding.stepBeta.greeting: Hi, I’m <david>David</david>! I build Cmdr, and you’re one of the very first people using it. Thanks for your trust! ❤️
onboarding.stepBeta.openBeta: Cmdr is in open beta: it’s overall solid and usable, but some parts are rough. <alpha></alpha> badges mark the most work-in-progress areas. Your feedback helps me fix bugs and prioritize features.
onboarding.stepBeta.checklist.title: Onboarding checklist, each takes 30 seconds:
onboarding.stepBeta.checklist.starNote: Homebrew needs Cmdr to have 225 stars to enable brew install cmdr
onboarding.stepBeta.checklist.alternativ: At the very top of the page, next to the “Cmdr” title. This helps people and Google notice Cmdr!
onboarding.stepBeta.checklist.email: Enter your email address <field></field> to get very occasional updates and questions
onboarding.stepBeta.analyticsLede:
To learn what’s working and what isn’t, during the open beta Cmdr sends usage stats: which features get used and how often, never anything from your files.
They’re tied to a random id, not to your name or email.
It’s on now, and you can turn it off anytime.
onboarding.stepBeta.analyticsCaption:
Note that it’s ON by default to encourage people to send me data during the Beta.
You can change this any time in Settings.
onboarding.stepBeta.crashReportsNote:
Crash reports are on too: if Cmdr goes down, it sends the app version, your macOS version, and where the code stopped.
Never your files.
You can turn both of these off in Settings whenever you like.
onboarding.stepBeta.analyticsManaged: Your organization turned off usage stats.
onboarding.stepBeta.crashReportsNoteAlon:
Crash reports are on: if Cmdr goes down, it sends the app version, your macOS version, and where the code stopped.
Never your files.
You can turn them off in Settings whenever you like.
onboarding.stepBeta.signup.success: Check your inbox to confirm your email. Thanks for helping out!
onboarding.stepBeta.signup.failure: Sorry, we couldn’t sign you up right now. Try again?
onboarding.stepBeta.signup.rejected: The mailing list didn’t accept that address. Worth a look for a typo, then hit Save again.
onboarding.stepBeta.signup.unreachable: Couldn’t reach the signup server just now, so you’re not on the list yet. Your address is saved on this Mac: hit Save again in a minute, or any time from Settings › Updates & privacy.
onboarding.stepBeta.emailNote:
Drop your email and I’ll reach out with the occasional question or update.
The email address you enter here is stored only on your Mac and it’s never connected to your usage stats, the two are intentionally two separate subsystems.
onboarding.stepBeta.terms.title: Oh, and this too please
onboarding.stepBeta.terms.lede: It’s a legal obligation to have it here.
onboarding.stepBeta.terms.consent: I’ve read and agree to the <terms>terms and conditions</terms>.
onboarding.stepBeta.terms.blockedTooltip: Accept the terms and conditions to continue.
onboarding.stepOptional.title: You’re almost ready
onboarding.stepOptional.lede: You chose to walk through a detailed setup, so here are a few quick choices. If you don’t care too much, click the button below. All of these are optional, and the defaults are picked for your benefit.
onboarding.stepOptional.changeAnytime: You can change this any time in Settings.
onboarding.stepOptional.networking.title: Networking
onboarding.stepOptional.networking.desc: Having this on means you can connect to SMB servers like company network shares, a home NAS, and the like. The only cost is a macOS permission dialog that pops up and asks you to allow “Local Network”, and one for “Accepting incoming connections”. Both dialogs are harmless, but if you don’t know what these are, they might be scary or annoying.
onboarding.stepOptional.indexing.title: Drive indexing
onboarding.stepOptional.indexing.summary: Takes 1 GB space, speeds up searches, shows folder sizes
onboarding.stepOptional.indexing.descInt: Drive indexing is totally cool! Gives you two main things:
onboarding.stepOptional.indexing.benefit: Instant search of your whole drive. Think Spotlight, but even faster.
Real-time folder sizes for your whole drive. You always know how much stuff you have in each folder.
onboarding.stepOptional.indexing.descCos: If you turn this off, you only get {dirPlaceholder} for the sizes. The cost is around 1 GB of index on your drive for a few million files, but no extra CPU or memory use after the first 2–3 minutes of you first starting the app, or starting it after a long time. It’s a cheap feature considering the benefits.
onboarding.stepOptional.updates.title: Automatic updates
onboarding.stepOptional.updates.summary: One tiny check at app start and once a day, so you stay on the latest version
onboarding.stepOptional.updates.desc:
If you enable this, Cmdr makes a tiny network request to a central license server at each app start plus once every 24 hours, and you always get the latest updates.
If you disable it, you keep your current version, and Cmdr makes zero automated network requests (except for periodic license checks, if you have a commercial license).
onboarding.stepOptional.mtp.title: MTP (Android phones, Kindles, cameras)
onboarding.stepOptional.mtp.summary: Lets you connect Android phones and the such, suppresses macOS native handler
onboarding.stepOptional.mtp.desc: If you enable this, Cmdr can connect to Android phones, Kindles, cameras, some music players, and any other device that supports the protocols called MTP or PTP. The cost is that macOS also wants to connect to these (and it usually fails, which is why you can’t just use Finder to copy photos from Android phones), so Cmdr has to suppress that macOS process while it’s running. When you quit Cmdr, this is politely restored.
onboarding.cloudSetup.title: Set up {provider}
onboarding.cloudSetup.step.signup: Sign up at <signupLink>{provider}</signupLink> (if you don’t have an account)
onboarding.cloudSetup.step.ollamaModel: Pull a model in a terminal with ollama pull llama3.2, or <libraryLink>browse the library</libraryLink>
onboarding.cloudSetup.step.lmStudioServe: Load a model in LM Studio, then start its <serverLink>local server</serverLink>
onboarding.cloudSetup.hint.azureEndpoint: Replace the placeholder in the address with your own Azure OpenAI resource name. This endpoint needs no api-version parameter.
onboarding.cloudSetup.hint.azureModel: On Azure this is your deployment name, which can differ from the name of the model it runs.
Your key is saved. Type a new one to replace it.
onboarding.cloudSetup.status.connectionE: Can’t reach the service right now
onboarding.cloudSetup.status.timedOut: The service is taking too long to answer. Try again in a moment.
onboarding.cloudSetup.status.invalidEndp: That address doesn’t look right. It should start with https://.
onboarding.cloudSetup.status.insecureEnd: Your key only travels over a secure connection, so use an address starting with https://.
onboarding.cloudSetup.status.providerRef: The service turned the request down (code {status}).
